threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the Dalston Junction steps like a tourist—locals glide up and down without a second thought.
Last night on the 333, a guy pulled out a saxophone and started playing a smooth jazz solo. Everyone just sat back like it was the most normal thing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I spotted an old couple arguing over the best döner place at the street corner while their parrot watched from a balcony. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can order currywurst with vegan options at 3 AM here, and the stands are packed. Only in Berlin will you find late-night food that’s both iconic and inclusive.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they’ve mastered the art of dodging those uneven sidewalk tiles without missing a beat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a lady juggling on the 14 bus this morning while a guy in a suit tried to tune her out with his earbuds. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Many tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it’s actually the neighborhood's quirky alleys and independent shops that pulse with local life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order coffee—still asking for 'café con leche' instead of just 'café'. It’s the small things.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the High Road' instead of just 'the road' when talking about Lea Bridge. Only locals know it’s a vibe, not just a route.
Saw a bloke on the 3 bus serenading the driver with a ukulele. Driver just shook his head, but it made the whole ride feel like a scene from a film.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy selling homemade falafel from his bike, while the Turkish grandmas argued over who makes it best at the market.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you'll find old-school Kiosk owners who know your name and what you usually buy—where else can you get a personal touch with your 5€ beer?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Real locals know to carry a reusable bag at all times. Tourists scramble to buy overpriced ones at the corner store when they hit the farmers market.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Spotted a man in a full tuxedo boarding the 21 Hayes—just another Tuesday in the Tenderloin, I guess. The city knows how to keep things interesting.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all Gràcia bars serve tapas, but many just vibe with vermut and unpretentious pintxos. The locals know where to find the real gems.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still avoid talking to the elderly in the park, too caught up in their phones and maps.
